c: Read the scenario and identify what is being targeted: confidentiality, integrity or availability.
Use exact J277 terminology: phishing, malware, brute-force, interception, DoS or SQL injection.
Choose a measure that counters the threat: education, updates, anti-malware, access rights, encryption, authentication, lockout or firewall.
An exam-quality answer says what a control does and why that interrupts the particular attack. Avoid simply listing security products.

m.title: Fake staff account alert
m.q: A pupil receives a fraudulent email asking them to sign into a fake school portal. Explain the threat and TWO ways to reduce the risk. [4 marks]
st: The email pretends to be trusted and asks for login credentials.
Phishing is a deceptive message intended to steal account details [1].
Training users to spot false links and unusual requests [1] can reduce unsafe clicks [1].
Two-factor authentication adds another check [1] so a stolen password alone may not allow access. Four teacher marking points are distributed across the explanation.

w: A school account is receiving repeated incorrect passwords. Explain two security controls that limit the attack. [4 marks]

An account lockout stops repeated attempts after a threshold [1], limiting brute-force guesses [1]. Two-factor authentication requires another proof of identity [1], so a guessed password alone is insufficient [1].
A laptop downloads harmful software. Explain two defences that could reduce damage. [4 marks]

Anti-malware detects/quarantines the threat [1], reducing malicious activity [1]. Restricted user access rights prevent ordinary accounts making system-wide changes [1], limiting potential damage [1].
A school's online service is overloaded with requests. Identify the threat and explain one suitable defence. [4 marks]
It is a denial-of-service attack [1] using excessive traffic/requests [1]. Firewall/rate limiting can filter or restrict unwanted traffic [1], helping keep service available to legitimate users [1].

k.q: Write a safe defensive decision program based on a previously classified security alert.
k.code:
alertLevel = 2
if alertLevel > 1 then
    print("Tell the IT team")
else
    print("Continue checking")
endif
p: Add print("Do not share passwords") at the end.
k.a:
At 2: Tell the IT team. At 0: Continue checking.

Extended OCR ERL:
alertLevel = 0
if alertLevel > 1 then
    print("Tell the IT team")
else
    print("Continue checking")
endif

An employee uses unprotected public Wi-Fi for confidential information. Explain the risk and a suitable control. [4 marks]

Source: Original J277-style question; not an OCR past-paper original.
Data could be intercepted during transmission [1] and private details read [1]. Encryption protects content in transit [1] so an interceptor without the key cannot understand it [1].

A school faces phishing, malware and brute-force login attempts. Describe one suitable protection for each and how it helps. [6 marks]

Source: Original J277-style question; not an OCR past-paper original.

Phishing: awareness training [1] reduces risky link clicks [1]. Malware: anti-malware software [1] detects/quarantines malicious programs [1]. Brute-force: account lockout [1] limits repeated password attempts [1]. Other correctly justified measures acceptable.
v: Keeping information private from unauthorised readers.
Keeping data accurate and protected against unauthorised change.
Making systems and data accessible to legitimate users.
Blocking repeated login attempts after failures.
Filters network traffic according to rules.
Makes transmitted data unreadable without the correct key.
x: Choosing security measures should depend on the particular threat described.
r: State what encryption does to data. [2 marks]
Transforms readable plaintext [1] into unreadable ciphertext without the correct key [1].
Monitors/filters network traffic [1] according to rules to block unauthorised traffic [1].
Attempts many possible passwords [1] to discover the correct one/gain access [1].
Explain how ransomware could disrupt a school. [4 marks]
Ransomware infects a device [1] and encrypts or locks files [1]. Teachers/pupils cannot access their work [1] and learning/administration may be disrupted [1].
